# Guided AI GRC Build: Proposal for Tamarack Instruments (fictional)

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel and Sponsor
**Program:** Guided AI GRC Build, 12 weeks, US$60,000
**Basis:** Client Profile Block v1.0 and discovery call notes of 6 October 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States, with about 1,100 staff. The Profile Block lists three AI use cases:

- A deployed customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- AI visual inspection, in pilot on the German production line.
- AI sales forecasting, planned for next year.

AI maturity is recorded as Piloting. The regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. ISO/IEC 42001 is a certification target, with work to start next year and no fixed start date. The incumbent frameworks are an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS, an ISO 9001 quality management system and an internal audit function. The Profile Block records an internal audit finding from June 2026: no inventory of AI systems.

Dana Whitfield stated the objective: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." The stated constraints are:

- Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026.

## 2. Why a Guided Build Rather Than Consulting Delivery

A consulting engagement typically hands over finished documents. The Client then has to absorb, adopt and operate them without the people who wrote them. The Guided AI GRC Build reverses that arrangement.

Your build team writes the charter, populates the inventory, runs the assessments and operates the evidence cycles. We provide the method, the frameworks, weekly coaching and quality review. When Week 12 closes, the people who built the system are the people who run it. They understand why each control exists, and they can extend the system to new use cases, such as the planned sales forecasting, without returning to an outside party.

The program works from two open frameworks:

- **GRC Workbook** (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) for governance, risk and compliance structures.
- **Slow AI Kitchen** (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen) for governed workflows and human oversight.

Steering material draws on **AI Governance for Boards** (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

Three principles guide every design choice:

- Slow AI
- Informed Intent
- Final Liability rests with the Human

## 3. Contracted Outcome: Minimum Viable AIMS at Week 12

The program contracts for a functioning minimum viable Artificial Intelligence Management System with six elements:

1. Adopted charter.
2. Populated inventory.
3. Operating risk register.
4. Adopted core policy set.
5. At least two governed AI workflows in production use.
6. Evidence collection running for at least four weeks.

The Profile Block lists one deployed system, the customer service chatbot. Which second workflow will be in production use by Week 12 is `Unknown`. This is the first question we will confirm at intake, because element 5 depends on it.

## 4. The Twelve-Week Spine, Tailored

**Inventory sequence.** In Week 2, the three systems in the Profile Block enter the inventory first:

- **Customer service chatbot**, because it is listed as deployed.
- **Visual inspection pilot**, because it is tied to the stated Q2 2027 objective.
- **Sales forecasting**, because entering a planned system at design stage lets it be governed from the start.

A discovery sweep for any further AI use then follows. This sweep responds directly to the June 2026 finding.

**ISO/IEC 42001 mapping.** The ISO/IEC 42001 column below shows readiness themes only. The program does not promise certification, audit or regulatory outcomes.

**Integration with incumbent frameworks.** Integration points with the ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS, the ISO 9001 quality management system and the internal audit function are marked `Unknown`. The Profile Block does not state which registers, procedures or records those frameworks hold. We will confirm them at intake so the AIMS attaches to existing structures rather than running in parallel.

| Week | Proposed work for Tamarack Instruments | ISO/IEC 42001 readiness theme | Integration point |
|---|---|---|---|
| W1 | Mobilization, AIMS charter draft, role assignments across the build team, works council consultation plan, steering checkpoint 1 | Clauses 4 and 5: context, scope, leadership; Annex A internal organization | `Unknown` |
| W2 | AI system inventory: chatbot, visual inspection pilot and sales forecasting first, then discovery sweep | Clause 4 scope; Annex A resources | `Unknown` |
| W3 | Classification and risk methodology, including EU AI Act classification and GDPR relevance per system (confirm with external counsel) | Clause 6.1 risk criteria | `Unknown` |
| W4 | Risk and impact assessments, chatbot and visual inspection first; data residency check against the EU customer data constraint | Clause 6.1 and 8; Annex A assessing impacts, data | `Unknown` |
| W5 | Risk register and treatment plans | Clause 6.1 treatment; Clause 8 | `Unknown` |
| W6 | Core policy set drafted for adoption; mid-point steering checkpoint 2 | Clause 5.2 AI policy; Annex A policies | `Unknown` |
| W7 | Operating procedures and lifecycle governance, including pilot-to-production gate for visual inspection and design gate for sales forecasting | Clause 8; Annex A lifecycle | `Unknown` |
| W8 | Vendor and supplier governance, including data residency terms; evidence collection starts | Annex A third-party relationships; Clause 7.5 | `Unknown` |
| W9 | Governed workflows and human oversight using Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen) | Clause 8; Annex A use of AI systems | `Unknown` |
| W10 | Testing, evaluation and monitoring | Clause 9.1 | `Unknown` |
| W11 | Incident response, change management, evidence review | Clauses 8 and 10 | `Unknown` |
| W12 | Audit readiness review, evidence walkthrough, closing steering checkpoint 3 | Clauses 9.2 and 9.3 readiness | `Unknown` |

Starting evidence collection in Week 8 provides five weeks of running evidence by Week 12. This meets the four-week minimum.

**Timing.** Twelve weeks starting in early January 2027 would place Week 12 before the start of Q2 2027. The actual start date is `Unknown` and will be set at contracting.

## 5. Client Team Commitment (Estimates)

The program assumes a standing build team drawn from the Audience Roles in the Profile Block. The weekly hours below are estimates covering the workshop, the coaching session and asynchronous work. Actual effort will be tracked during the program.

| Role | Typical week, hours (estimate) | Peak weeks | Peak week, hours (estimate) |
|---|---|---|---|
| General Counsel | 3 to 4 | W1, W3, W6 | 5 to 6 |
| CISO | 3 to 4 | W4, W8, W11 | 5 to 6 |
| Head of Quality | 4 to 5 | W5, W7, W10 | 6 to 7 |
| Head of Data | 4 to 6 | W2, W4, W10 | 7 to 8 |
| German plant manager | 2 to 3 | W4, W7, W9 | 4 to 5 |
| Internal auditor 1 | 2 | W11, W12 | 4 |
| Internal auditor 2 | 2 | W11, W12 | 4 |

Two questions for intake:

- **Internal audit role.** We propose that the two internal auditors take an advisory and assurance role rather than an implementation role, to protect audit independence. Please confirm this suits the internal audit function.
- **Program coordinator.** Which team member will act as program coordinator? This role adds an estimated 2 hours per week.

## 6. Steering Cadence

Executive steering checkpoints take place at three points:

- **Week 1:** mobilization brief covering scope, team, delivery risks and decisions needed.
- **Week 6:** mid-point report covering spine status, artifact register excerpt, blockers and scope decisions.
- **Week 12:** closing report with a minimum viable AIMS attestation against the six elements, an evidence sample index and a 12-month operating plan.

We propose that Dana Whitfield, as Sponsor, convenes each checkpoint. Steering attendance is `Unknown` and will be confirmed at intake.

## 7. Logistics and Price

**Delivery format.** All sessions are virtual. Each week includes one live workshop, one coaching session and structured asynchronous implementation between sessions. Session times will be set once participant time zones are confirmed at intake.

**Price.** US$60,000 for the twelve-week program. This sits within the US$80,000 budget approval stated in the Profile Block. Whether the program start date falls within the fiscal year covered by that approval is `Unknown` and will be confirmed at intake.

**Contract terms.** Payment schedule and terms will be set out in the statement of work. Confirm with external counsel.

## 8. Questions to Confirm at Intake

1. Which second AI workflow is expected to be in production use by Week 12?
2. Does the works council consultation requirement apply to the visual inspection pilot, and what lead time does consultation need? Confirm with external counsel.
3. Which ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and ISO 9001 quality management system artifacts, such as risk registers, supplier procedures, document control or incident processes, should the AIMS attach to?
4. Does the chatbot or any planned system process customer data, and where is that data stored and processed?
5. Who will attend the steering checkpoints, and which team member will serve as program coordinator?

## 9. Next Step

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. We propose a short intake call to work through the questions above. We will then issue a statement of work with a confirmed start date. Confirm with external counsel.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.

'This sweep responds directly to the June 2026 finding' links proposed work to a Profile Block risk event. I treated it as proposed work rather than a described Client state.

'We propose that Dana Whitfield, as Sponsor, convenes each checkpoint' touches guardrail 7 on who attends what. I treated it as a proposal, and the text renders attendance `Unknown`. Another scorer might read it as an inferred relation.

The generic statement that a consulting engagement 'typically hands over finished documents' describes consulting, not the Client or an invented statistic. I did not count it as a fail.
